title: Recordings and course reports: ideas from other products
intro: This page shows examples from other products for recordings and course reports in Essentials 2.0, under Courses, with a hand-off to the Learner Portal. It covers two related tasks: organising and sharing sensitive session recordings, and understanding course and learner results. The screenshots show what those products display. If a screenshot does not show a feature, that does not mean the product lacks it. The examples come from the design reference libraries Mobbin and Refero.

questions.title: How are recordings organised and searched by event, learner or scenario?
questions.answer: Loom combines broad library search, folders and recording cards with lots of detail. Vimeo highlights recent videos and keeps a search field always available. Zoom has the strongest grouping by event: several recording files sit under one named meeting. For Essentials, combine that session bundle with searchable event, learner and scenario details. Organising along those three axes is a proposal here, not something these screenshots show.

questions.title: Who can access recordings, and can access be limited by group or time?
questions.answer: Vimeo separates link privacy from named collaborator roles. Zoom shows audience settings, a passcode and an optional expiration checkbox (shown unchecked), and the screenshots reach a saved update. Loom's share dialog shows 'Anyone with the link can view'; for sensitive debrief footage that is an example of what not to do, not proof of Loom's usual default. Essentials should make the recording audience clear and easy to review. These screenshots do not show automatic learner-own-only access or course-group rules.

questions.title: What playback extras help review, and how do they relate to Elevate's AI video annotation and chapters?
questions.answer: Grain links selected transcript text to a timestamped comment and a reply box. Loom shows an editable AI summary and chapter list. Vimeo's 'No speech detected' message shows the need for a fallback when there is no transcript. Apply these patterns to Elevate's AI video annotation and chapter work: editable scenario phases, shared times for comments and chapters, and a clear note that AI produced them. The screenshots do not show seeking behaviour, AI accuracy or competency scoring.

questions.title: How is a report structured from overview to learner detail to export?
questions.answer: The full reporting path is pieced together from several products. Circle shows course summaries, a student table and an export. Kajabi shows detail from learner to course to module to lesson. SchoolAI puts class outcomes and learner insights next to a CSV download. No single set of screenshots shows overview, then learner detail, then export end to end. Essentials should keep course and filter context at each level, and limit export to the report on screen; that is a design proposal.

questions.title: Which metrics appear by default, and can cohorts be compared?
questions.answer: Completion and mastery are separate in these examples. Circle reports average course completion, Kajabi shows lesson completion, and SchoolAI labels outcome and mastery measures. Mixpanel makes metric definitions, date ranges, filters and cohort breakdowns visible, but its retention and event counts measure behaviour, not learning. Coursera's Grades screen shows assessment scores. Borrow comparison controls while keeping attendance, completion, score and mastery separate. Default attendance and a shared basis for comparing cohorts across assessments are gaps in this evidence.

questions.title: How do learners see their own results in a simpler view?
questions.answer: Coursera separates a short personal progress summary from assessment detail. The Grades view shows overall pass or grade plus each assessment's status, due date, weight and grade. Mobile emphasises completion and next work. Essentials can use this personal view for released results and recordings, with a path back to the relevant simulation moment. These screenshots do not show learner recording access or a shared instructor and learner data model. Only one product covers the learner side, so this report does not claim that products agree here.

references.title: Searchable Loom recording library
references.question: Q1
references.take: Loom's recording library is a searchable index with thumbnails for finding recorded sessions.

references.title: Compact Loom recordings list
references.question: Q1
references.take: A compact recordings list uses how recent a video is and its thumbnail so people can find a course session.

references.title: Loom video list view
references.question: Q1
references.take: The list view lets people scan many recordings as a collection instead of opening one video at a time.

references.title: Loom recording detail on iOS
references.question: Q1
references.take: The mobile detail screen gives a short path from a recording to playback or sharing.

references.title: Vimeo video content library
references.question: Q1
references.take: Vimeo's content library keeps navigation and search available, with cards and pagination for browsing a large video collection.

references.title: Vimeo video platform dashboard
references.question: Q1
references.take: A second Vimeo screenshot shows library browsing with a clear content area, search and card-based discovery.

references.title: Sharing a Zoom recording
references.question: Q1
references.take: An eight-screen sequence shows finding a recording, opening share controls, choosing who can access it, and finishing distribution.

references.title: Loom sharing controls
references.question: Q2
references.take: Loom's share dialog lets you pick named or workspace recipients, while the link setting shown is 'Anyone with the link can view'. For sensitive debriefs, that broad setting needs a careful review.

references.title: Vimeo privacy settings
references.question: Q2
references.take: Vimeo shows recording privacy controls at the point where an instructor chooses who can view a video.

references.title: Vimeo sharing options
references.question: Q2
references.take: A separate sharing options screen supports careful distribution choices for sensitive course footage.

references.title: Zoom recording access
references.question: Q2
references.take: Zoom provides an access screen for limiting recordings to the intended participants.

references.title: Zoom recording permissions
references.question: Q2
references.take: Zoom's permissions screen is a useful reference for learner-only or group-limited recording access.

references.title: Updating Zoom share settings
references.question: Q2
references.take: Zoom share settings screens show audience, passcode and an unchecked expiration option, then a confirmation that settings were updated. They do not show learner-own-only access or course-group rules.

references.title: Adding a Grain comment
references.question: Q3
references.take: Five screens in order link transcript text to a timestamped comment and a reply box. The screenshots skip intermediate clicks and playback seeking.

references.title: Loom video player
references.question: Q3
references.take: Loom's player pairs the video with a transcript and collaboration tools for review by time.

references.title: Playback with transcript and comment
references.question: Q3
references.take: Loom shows a timestamped transcript, search and copy controls, and a Comment action beside playback. Comment submission and jumping from the transcript are not shown.

references.title: Loom AI summary and chapters
references.question: Q3
references.take: Loom shows an editable summary and timestamped chapters next to a note that AI generated the content. How generation and saving work are not shown.

references.title: Vimeo video player
references.question: Q3
references.take: Vimeo's player page is a focused layout that works well with chapters and a transcript beside the video.

references.title: Vimeo playback detail
references.question: Q3
references.take: Vimeo's detail view is a useful reference for keeping metadata and playback controls near the video.

references.title: Vimeo when no speech is detected
references.question: Q3
references.take: Vimeo's transcript panel says 'No speech detected', which shows the need for a useful fallback when speech tools cannot run.

references.title: Circle course analytics
references.question: Q4
references.take: Circle analytics starts with a course-level overview as the way into learner performance reporting.

references.title: Exporting Circle students
references.question: Q4
references.take: Circle screens show a course student table, an export menu and an email-delivery confirmation. Steps between them and the export choices are not shown.

references.title: Learner detail by course, module and lesson
references.question: Q4
references.take: Kajabi places overall progress, last activity, module progress and lesson completion under a course and learner breadcrumb. How you arrive there and export are not shown.

references.title: SchoolAI report overview
references.question: Q4
references.take: SchoolAI is a direct education reporting example with an overview suited to instructor review.

references.title: Downloading a SchoolAI report
references.question: Q4
references.take: SchoolAI report screens show generated learner and session insights, 'Download CSV' and a short success message. The CSV itself and a move to learner detail are not shown.

references.title: Uxcel learner analytics
references.question: Q4
references.take: Uxcel shows a learner-focused analytics view that can inform how drill-down is structured.

references.title: Mixpanel analytics dashboard
references.question: Q5
references.take: An analytics overview makes the measured event and time range visible before comparing performance. That helps keep outcome measures separate from engagement proxies.

references.title: Mixpanel report segmentation
references.question: Q5
references.take: Mixpanel shows named behaviour metrics, date range, filters and cohort breakdowns. Comparable engagement does not mean comparable learning outcomes.

references.title: Mixpanel retention comparison
references.question: Q5
references.take: A cohort chart supports reading trends side by side. Retention is an engagement proxy and should sit beside completion, attendance, score or mastery evidence.

references.title: View retained users
references.question: Q5
references.take: The sequence moves from an overview into retained-user detail, showing a useful path from a cohort signal to inspecting a learner.

references.title: Exporting Mixpanel events
references.question: Q5
references.take: The export flow is a concrete hand-off for further cohort analysis when reports need to be shared or audited.

references.title: Coursera learner course view
references.question: Q6
references.take: The learner course view puts progress through content first, giving a simpler personal view of course status.

references.title: Coursera completed work
references.question: Q6
references.take: Completed items appear as a learner-facing status list. That outcome summary avoids showing instructor cohort complexity.

references.title: Course overview and upcoming graded work
references.question: Q6
references.take: Coursera's course overview shows workload, objectives, deadlines and upcoming graded work. This is planning context, not an assessment result.

references.title: Learner Grades with weighted assessments
references.question: Q6
references.take: Coursera's learner Grades view shows overall pass or grade plus assessment status, due date, weight and grade. It does not show competency mastery.

references.title: Coursera iOS progress
references.question: Q6
references.take: The iOS learner view shows that progress and course status can stay the main structure on mobile.

references.title: Coursera iOS result detail
references.question: Q6
references.take: A compact mobile result detail keeps learner feedback available without copying the instructor report screen.
